scope: Synthetic scalar readout component comparison; not R2, PC-ALM replication or evidence of an SNN advantage
method: Each seed assigns random binary targets to 16 route IDs. Same deterministic route/delay/noise stream is used by every arm. Warmup precedes scored predict-then-feedback episodes. Stationary and reversal are noiseless; reversal flips every 256 scored episodes. Noisy flips labels with probability 0.2. Delay alternates randomly between 1 and 8 ticks; expired_feedback uses 80 ticks. Each episode starts 100 ticks after the preceding one. Single supplied route has eligibility 1. Shuffled receives an independent balanced outcome. Frozen remains zero. scalar_ema uses a non-spiking scalar error update at the same rate and delay attenuation. No hyperparameter tuning on these seeds. Score is clipped to [-1,1], p=(score+1)/2, prediction=(score>0). Brier is (p-label)^2. Accuracy and Brier are computed before feedback. Aggregate each scenario and seed equally; exclude expired_feedback from utility means, and require it to produce no updates. Store per-seed metrics, full deterministic trace digest, source hashes and resource observations. Select residual only if its gain threshold and every scenario accuracy tolerance pass; select integrated only if the residual gate and its own threshold, every scenario Brier tolerance and all positive seed gains pass. Otherwise retain three_factor. Scalar parity is not an SNN advantage. One exclusive result artifact per protocol; failed runs consume the attempt.
